To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TIPS in liver transplant recipients is safe and effective but less efficacious than in nontransplant recipients.

TIPS insertion is a feasible option in OLT patients with complications of portal hypertension but that the efficacy is lower than in nontransplant patients, and the outcomes are poor in the OLT patients with a preprocedural MELD score greater than 15.
TIPS in OLT patients has a lower technical and clinical success rate than TIPS in non‐OLT patients.

TIPS is not recommended for the treatment of refractory ascites or bleeding in OLT recipients, and the role of TIPS for the treatment of these complications in nontransplant patients remains unclear.
TIPS is not recommended for the treatment of portal hypertensive complications in liver transplant patients.
TIPS insertion is not recommended for patients who have undergone liver transplantation.
